The Petitioners have filed the IA Dy No. 96/2026 seeking the following reliefs: - _(a) Take on record the subsequent event, namely the revocation letter dated 11.02.2026 issued by Respondent No.1;_ - _(b) Direct that the operation and effect of the revocation letter dated 11.02.2026 be kept in abeyance pending pronouncement of the order in Petition No. 1015/MP/2025 and IA No. 5/2026;_ - _(c) Pass such other and further orders as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice._ - _“2. After hearing the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed as under:_ _(b)The Respondents to file their replies, if any, within three weeks with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder(s), if any, within three weeks thereafter._ _(c)The Respondent, CTUIL, to also clarify, on an affidavit, as to whether intimation of final grant of connectivity has been issued to the Petitioner, if not, the reasons for the same and what is the status of implementation of transmission system for the connectivity of the Petitioner, within two weeks._ _2. At the request of the learned senior counsel and learned counsel for the parties, the Commission also permitted both sides to file their respective written submissions within two days with a copy to the other side._ _3. Since the parties argued the matter on the merits, the Commission deemed it appropriate to reserve the matter itself for the order.”_ reserved for orders. The Petitioner has submitted that such action has been taken on the same grounds which are under adjudication, including the issue of Financial Closure timeline and permissibility of coercive action, and therefore amounts to preempting the decision of this Hon’ble Commission and undermining the adjudicatory process. It has been contended that the said revocation renders the pending proceedings infructuous and defeats the reliefs sought in the Petition. _“Learned senior counsel for the Petitioner, DPIPL, submitted that the present IA has been filed inter alia seeking direction to the Respondent, CTUIL, to keep the revocation letter dated 11.2.2026 in abeyance pending orders of the Commission in Petition No. 1015/MP/2025. The learned senior counsel further submitted that the filing of the present IA became necessitated owing to the fact that the Respondent, notwithstanding that the matter had been fully heard and reserved for orders by the Commission, has proceeded to revoke the Petitioner’s connectivity vide email dated 11.2.2026, without awaiting the decision of the Commission. The learned senior counsel submitted that the very grounds forming the basis of the said revocation are identical to those which are under consideration in the pending proceedings, and that the action of the Respondent in revoking the Petitioner’s connectivity during the period when the matter stood reserved for orders is ex facie arbitrary and thereby rendering the main Petition infructuous and defeating the reliefs sought therein. The learned senior counsel added that, pursuant to the issuance of the revocation notice, the Petitioner, in compliance with Regulation 3.8 of the GNA Regulations, has deposited an amount equivalent to the Connectivity Bank Guarantee under express protest and solely with a view to securing the Connectivity Bank Guarantee from encashment._ _2. In response, the learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, fairly submitted that the Commission has, in similar cases, restrained the creation of third-party rights over the revoked quantum pending the pronouncement of the order, and CTUIL has no objection if a similar dispensation is adopted in this case too._ _3. Considering the submissions made by the learned senior counsel and learned counsel for the parties, the Commission directed CTUIL not to re-allocate the quantum corresponding to the Petitioner’s 162 MW connectivity at Dhule PS to any third parties till the pronouncement of the order in the Petition. With this, IA (Diary) No. 96/2026 was disposed of.”_ 13. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, Respondent and perused the facts available on record. title: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) and 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 41 and 42 of the CERC (Connectivity and General Network access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations 2022 (as amended) seeking Extension in respect to timeline for achieving Financial Closure as a "condition subsequent" to be satisfied by the Connectivity Grantee under Regulation 11A(2) thereof and extension of start date of connectivity pursuant to Regulation 11A(2A).
